title: Integrative taxonomy reveals three new Novibipalium species (Tricladida: Geoplanidae) from South Korea, with notes on morphological variation and parasitism
content:
Abstract
Land planarians (Platyhelminthes: Geoplanidae) are highly sensitive to microhabitat changes and possess low vagility, making them excellent indicators of ecological health. Despite the severe environmental degradation of the Korean Peninsula during the 20th century, recent molecular surveys have suggested a surprisingly high, yet largely undescribed, diversity of species in the region. We employed an integrative taxonomic approach to characterize three new species of the genus Novibipalium collected from various regions of South Korea between 2020 and 2024. Morphological (histology) analyses were complemented by molecular phylogenetic inferences using a combined dataset of nuclear (18S, 28S rDNA) and mitochondrial (COI) genes, as well as automated species delimitation (ASAP algorithm). As a result, three new species were discovered and described: Novibipalium variabile sp. nov., which exhibits variation in external and internal traits, Novibipalium variabiliforme sp. nov., and Novibipalium jejuense sp. nov. Phylogenetic analyses and ASAP also support the identity of these new bipaliin taxa. Secondary, non-functional female organs in one specimen of N. jejuense sp. nov. are hypothesized to result from nematode infestation. These taxonomic findings increase the known diversity of Korean land planarians and highlight the importance of integrative taxonomy in identifying both morphologically variable and morphologically similar species.
